1. a standing place for animals, Lat. stabulum, a stable, fold, (Iliad by Homer): a stye , (Odyssey by Homer): of men, a dwelling, abode , (Hesiod) 
2. quarters, lodgings for travellers or soldiers, Lat. statio, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Persia, σταθμοί were stations on the royal road, where the king rested, (Herdotus Historicus): hence a day's journey, day's march , averaging about 5 parasangs or 15 miles,…
flour of spelt mixed and made into dough , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)
stiff fat, tallow, suet , Lat. sebum, opp. toπιμελή (Lat. adeps, soft fat), (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)
to cover , (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, ὕπνος στ. τινά covers, embraces one, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., πλοῖον ἐστεγασμένον a decked vessel, (Antipho Orator) (ML)

1. waterproof , (Herdotus Historicus); στεγνὰ οἰκήματα, of a cave, (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, στεγνόν, οῦ, a covered dwelling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
the crown of the root, stump , whence the trunk springs, Lat. codex, (Pindar) (ML)
